source_name: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 4 Chapter 11 (N2O from managed soils, CO2 from lime and urea)
read_from: Section 11.3.1 Equation 11.12 (printed page 11.27) and Section 11.4.1 Equation 11.13 (printed page 11.32), read from the published pages

conversion.note: The equations give CO2-C; the text of both sections says to multiply by 44/12 to express it as CO2.

limestone.unit: tonne of C per tonne of limestone (CaCO3)
limestone.note: Equation 11.12, Step 2: apply an overall emission factor of 0.12 for limestone. The uncertainty cannot exceed the factor itself, because it is the absolute maximum that can be released.

dolomite.unit: tonne of C per tonne of dolomite (CaMg(CO3)2)
dolomite.note: Equation 11.12, Step 2: apply an overall emission factor of 0.13 for dolomite.

urea.unit: tonne of C per tonne of urea
urea.note: Equation 11.13, Step 2: an emission factor of 0.20, which is the carbon content of urea on an atomic weight basis (20% for CO(NH2)2). The CO2 removed during manufacture is counted in the IPPU sector, which is why the application is reported here.

guidance.urea_in_solution: Where urea is applied in a fertiliser solution and the urea share is not known, Section 11.4.1 says it is good practice to treat the whole solution as urea rather than under-estimate.
guidance.urea_is_also_nitrogen: Urea applied to soil is both a CO2 source (this file) and a nitrogen input to Equation 11.1 (managed_soils.json). Both have to be reported; they are different gases, not a double count.
